 WTA Guangzhou Quarterfinal Predictions Including Paula Badosa vs Harriet Dart 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 The WTA Guangzhou Open is down to the last eight, with two Chinese youngsters still in the running to become the seventh Chinese woman to win this title. As always, we here at LWOT will be offering our predictions for every match on the slate, as well as the quarterfinals in Tokyo . Interestingly, all the matches are first-time encounters between the players involved, adding uncertainty to the outcome. But who will advance?
 WTA Guangzhou Quarterfinal Predictions
 Jil Teichmann vs Kaitlin Quevedo
 Head-to-head: first meeting
 Kaitlin Quevedo arrives in the WTA Guangzhou quarterfinals with momentum and a fresh title in her pocket. The 20-year-old held her nerve against Anna Bondar, saving nine of ten break points to win 7-5 6-3, after already toppling 2020 Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin in round one. She won her first tour-level trophy in Sao Paulo only last month, and she is already deep into another draw. That is not a fluke; that is a player learning to win.
 Jil Teichmann will not make it easy. The Swiss left-hander dropped the opener against sixth seed Zeynep Sonmez, then roared back 4-6 6-3 6-1, reminding everyone how dangerous she is on hard courts after her fourth-round run at Roland Garros. Expect a contest of resilience against resolve, but Quevedo’s form, composure under pressure and rising confidence give her the narrow edge to book a semifinal spot.
 Prediction: Quevedo in 3 
 Claire Liu vs Sun Xinran
 Head-to-head: first meeting
 Sun Xinran has arrived, and she did not wait for an invitation. The 16-year-old, fresh off the US Open juniors title, took down third seed Maria Timofeeva in a deciding-set tiebreak to reach her first tour-level quarterfinal. Add a straightforward opening win over Mananchaya Sawangkaew and a third-round run at the China Open, where only Coco Gauff could stop her, and the momentum is hard to ignore. Her fearless ball-striking has made her the story of the week in Guangzhou.
 Standing in her way is Claire Liu, who got here without hitting a ball after Katerina Siniakova’s withdrawal, and who is one win from a second straight semifinal at WTA Guangzhou. Fresh legs and a strong Guangzhou record give her a real edge. Equally, after her form so far this week, the Chinese player can’t be written off, and her sun will keep shining in this one.
 Prediction: Sun in 3 
 Mar 11, 2022; Indian Wells, CA, USA; Claire Liu (USA) hits a shot against Coco Gauff (not pictured) in her 2nd round match at the BNP Paribas Open at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-USA TODAY Sports 
 Lilli Tagger vs Shi Han
 Head-to-head: first meeting
 Lilli Tagger walks into this quarterfinal as the player with the bigger ceiling and the flashier toolkit. The Austrian teenager already has a maiden WTA title from Prague , has become the youngest player in the top 50, and has a one-handed backhand that few opponents know how to solve. Expect her to dictate from the first ball, use the slice to drag Han Shi out of position, and close points at the net. If her first serve holds up, this should be tidy.
 Han Shi has been here before and won’t be starstruck. Back in 2024, she came through a first-round win at WTA Guangzhou as a wildcard before falling to Bouzas Maneiro in the last 16, and this season she has come through qualifying to reach the third round at Wuhan. Her game is built on depth and patience, so her route is to stay in the rally, absorb the pace and wait for Tagger’s errors. Shi can steal a set, but it is hard to beat a teenager who is swinging freely.
 Prediction: Tagger in 3 
 Paula Badosa vs Harriet Dart
 Head-to-head: first meeting
 Paula Badosa is quietly rebuilding in Guangzhou. She looked particularly sharp in dispatching Sinja Kraus 6-1 6-4 in just 67 minutes, winning 82% of her first-serve points, after beating Carol Young Suh Lee by the same score in the first round. For a player chasing a strong finish to a frustrating 2026, with a run to the Iasi Open final the season’s brightest spot, this is exactly the kind of clean, clinical tennis she needs.
 Harriet Dart will not be so accommodating. The Briton has just knocked out second seed Janice Tjen 6-4 3-6 6-3, her second top-50 win of the year and her first tour-level quarter-final since Eastbourne in 2024. Badosa won their last meeting at the 2023 United Cup, and her serve and form make her the pick, but expect Dart to make her work for it.
 Prediction: Badosa in 3
